analyst.summary: The Leela's owner, Schloss Bangalore, used India's largest-ever hotel IPO in 2025 to pay down a large chunk of debt, and the numbers since have moved the right way - revenue and EBITDA both growing at double-digit rates, interest costs falling, and the company profitable for the first time after two loss-making years. The very low return-on-equity figure in our data reflects that recent history (new equity base, still-ramping profit) rather than a weak business - asset-level returns (ROCE) are already healthy. India's luxury hotel segment is in a strong up-cycle, which is helping room rates and occupancy. This is a story still proving itself post-IPO rather than a name with an established earnings track record, so we rate it a Hold.
